newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Alusaf Mozal project could start in October.
newsitem.headline: Alusaf Mozal project could start in October.

text.p: South African aluminium producer Alusaf Ltd said on Monday building of the $1.2 million Mozal aluminium smelter in Mozambique could begin in October this year.

The company, owned by Gencor Ltd, said in an advertisement in the daily Noticias a study from Alusaf was considering building the smelter in Boane district, about 40 km southwest of the capital Maputo.
"Construction of the smelter could begin in October 1997 and completion is envisaged in August 2000," the advertisement said.
The advertisement said the modern smelter would be "safe, efficient and environmentally friendly".
Alusaf said last month it had signed a "housekeeping" agreement with Mozambique on the construction of the smelter in March, but was tryng to cut costs to make the project commercially viable.
Gencor chairman Brian Gilbertson had requested Alusaf to try and report back to the company's board in June. Gilbertson said in February returns for the project were not attractive enough.
A study showed the Mozal project to be feasible with a capacity to produce 245,000 tonnes of aluminium a year for export with possible expansion to 490,000.
Alusaf owns and operates two aluminium smelters in South Africa's Indian Ocean port of Richards Bay.
